main_system_reason: The street blocks of the lower city are the planned layout of the town. On the 1967-68 plan their edges are square to each other within about two degrees, and the independently drawn 1968-69 plan gives the same direction for the same streets relative to its own north (sys5) within one degree.
notes: We measured the two settlement plans published in Indian Archaeology - A Review for 1967-68 (Fig. 7) and 1968-69, both drawn by the ASI from the 1960-69 excavations of Lal and Thapar. Both arrows are lettered only N. The excavation report on the structures (Excavations at Kalibangan: The Harappans, Part I) is not available to us; the locally held Part II covers finds and has no plans. Both plans place the street grid of the lower city (KLB-2) about fifteen degrees anticlockwise of the plan's north, and they agree on this within one degree although they were redrawn and their arrows differ greatly on the page. They disagree on the citadel (KLB-1) and the outline of the lower city. On the 1967-68 plan the southern half of the citadel is a rhomb: its east and west walls run within about five degrees of north while its cross wall lies parallel to the streets, and the west wall of the lower city is oblique to the streets. On the 1968-69 plan the citadel walls and the north wall of the lower city are parallel or square to the streets. The plans are schematic: streets are drawn as pairs of solid or dashed lines without a legend, and contours are superimposed. The 1967-68 figure is printed white on black and was measured on an inverted copy; the 1968-69 figure is a 565 x 807 px scan, so its lines are short in pixels and its errors larger.
